evidence: The whole solution is "For a fair coin, the probability of an odd number of tails in any number of tosses equals \\(\\frac{1}{2}\\) (the even and odd cases split the binomial expansion equally when \\(p = q = \\frac{1}{2}\\)). So \\(P(\\text{odd number of tails}) = \\frac{1}{2}\\)." There is no computation anywhere. The parenthetical asserts the equal split of the binomial expansion, and that assertion IS the entire content of the question — restating it is not deriving it. A student who did not already know the result learns nothing about why it holds, and cannot reproduce the argument on the next question of this shape.

Putting \\(x = 1\\) in \\((1+x)^{100}\\) gives \\(\\sum_k {}^{100}C_k = 2^{100}\\); putting \\(x = -1\\) gives \\(\\sum_k (-1)^k\\,{}^{100}C_k = 0\\). Adding and subtracting, \\(\\sum_{k \\text{ even}} {}^{100}C_k = \\sum_{k \\text{ odd}} {}^{100}C_k = 2^{99}\\). Hence \\(P(\\text{odd number of tails}) = \\frac{2^{99}}{2^{100}} = \\frac{1}{2}\\)." (Equivalently, the one-line argument: whatever the parity of the first 99 tosses, the 100th toss makes the total odd with probability exactly \\(\\frac{1}{2}\\).)
